newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin-Ciampi sees Italy growth of 1.5 pct at most.
newsitem.headline: Berlin-Ciampi sees Italy growth of 1.5 pct at most.

text.p: Italian Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Saturday he did not see Italy meeting an original forecast for two-percent 1997 growth.

"Italy will not meet its original two-percent growth goal for GDP in 1997. The trend has been positive in the last months, but the 1997 average growth will be above one percent and at most 1.5 percent," he told reporters after the Group of Seven (G7) of industrialised nations' meeting.
Ciampi said Italy's public sector deficit to gross domestic produtc (GDP) ratio would stand at 6.8 percent in 1996, according to new accounting methods approved by the Eurostat statistics office.
He added that the G7 meeting considered the slow economic upturn in Europe as a whole and a pick-up was seen in France and Germany.
Antonio Fazio, Italy's central bank governor, said European currency fluctuations at current levels were acceptable.
Both Ciampi and Fazio said Italy's outward credibility had grown.
